questions.q: What were the two main pillars of the economy during the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.a: The two main pillars were agriculture and trade. A student who misses this likely confuses the Sultanate's political structure (the ruling class) with how the actual people earned their daily living.

questions.q: Why did the Delhi Sultanate remain a diverse society despite being an Islamic state?
questions.a: It remained diverse because the majority of the population was Hindu, and most Sultans allowed them to practice their own religion. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks rulers always force their own religion on every single subject, missing the concept of religious coexistence.

questions.q: If a traveler arrived in a Sultanate city to sell spices, what role would the Sultanate government play in their business?
questions.a: The government would likely collect taxes from the trade, as land and trade taxes were the main revenue sources. This shows the student understands that the government's primary interaction with the economy was through taxation to support the state.

questions.q: How did the religious policy of the Sultans change the daily lives of the common people?
questions.a: It created a mixed environment where people practiced different faiths side-by-side, though there were occasional periods of intolerance. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks the society was completely uniform, ignoring the historical reality of a majority-Hindu population under a Muslim Sultan.

questions.q: Was the Delhi Sultanate a period of total cultural isolation? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, it was not, because trade flourished and different religious groups lived within the same borders. A wrong answer indicates the student views the Sultanate as a "closed box" rather than an active, trading society.

questions.q: Imagine you are a historian studying this time. What evidence would you look for to prove that different cultures were living together?
questions.a: I would look for archaeological remains of diverse places of worship, records of trade between different groups, and accounts of festivals. A poor answer would focus only on the Sultan's personal life, failing to see that history is found in the daily lives of all people.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Life under the Delhi Sultanate was a period where an Islamic ruling class governed a society that remained ______ Hindu, leading to a unique blend of cultural practices, agricultural reliance, and trade expansion.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you move to a new neighborhood where everyone has different ______, food, and festivals.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to describe how the Sultanate maintained political control while allowing religious diversity among their subjects.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you move to a new ______ where everyone has different traditions, food, and festivals.
